Web search results for ""FarDriver ND72450" parameter list Android app":

The **FarDriver ND72450** is a high-performance sine-wave controller commonly used for electric motorcycles and high-power e-bikes.[1] To program it, you need the official Android application and a Bluetooth dongle.

### 1. App Download
The official app is typically distributed as an APK file. You can download the latest version from the following sources:
*   **Official Download Link:** [http://182.92.233.85:6868/FarDriverSigned.apk](http://182.92.233.85:6868/FarDriverSigned.apk)[2]
*   **Alternative (MotoEV):** [https://www.motoev.net/download/MotoEV-Fardrive/APK/](https://www.motoev.net/download/MotoEV-Fardrive/APK/)[3]
*   **iOS Version:** Search for **"南京远驱"** (Nanjing Yuanqu) in the Apple App Store.

### 2. Key Parameter List for ND72450
Once connected via Bluetooth, the app allows you to modify several critical performance settings:

| Parameter | Description | Recommended/Max for ND72450 |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Max Phase Current** | Controls low-end torque and acceleration.[4] | **450A** (Hardware Limit) |
| **Max Line Current** | Controls total battery power draw. | **200A** (Hardware Limit) |
| **Rated Voltage** | Set based on your battery (e.g., 60V or 72V). | Max input: **88V - 90V** |
| **Low Voltage Protect** | Shuts off power to protect the battery. | Set to BMS cutoff (e.g., 63V for 72V) |
| **Over Voltage Protect** | Protects controller from high voltage spikes. | Typically **88V - 90V** |
| **Throttle Accel** | Sensitivity of the throttle response. | Range: 16–224 (Higher is punchier) |
| **Field Weakening** | Increases top speed by sacrificing efficiency. | Use with caution to avoid overheating. |
| **3-Speed Gear** | Sets power ratios for Low, Mid, and High modes. | e.g., 50%, 75%, 100% |
| **Auto-Learn** | Calibrates the motor's hall sensors and angle. | **Must run** during first setup. |

### 3. Connection Steps
1.  **Hardware:** Plug the FarDriver Bluetooth dongle into the controller's 10-pin or 6-pin diagnostic port.
2.  **Power:** Turn on the bike's ignition (the controller must be powered).
3.  **App:** Open the FarDriver app, click **"Connect"** or **"Scan"**, and select the device (often named "Yuyangking" or similar).
4.  **Communication:** Once the status shows "Connected" or "Bound," you can read and write parameters.

### ⚠️ Safety Warning
*   **Backup Settings:** Always take a screenshot of your original settings before making changes.
*   **Phase Current:** Setting the phase current too high for your motor can melt wires or damage the motor magnets.
*   **Field Weakening:** Excessive field weakening can cause the motor to spin at dangerous RPMs or cause the controller to fail if the battery disconnects during high-speed regen.

Web search results for ""FarDriver" controller manual AND "parameter list" Android app filetype:pdf OR tuning guide":

For the **FarDriver (Nanjing Remote Drive)** controller, the most comprehensive resources include the official factory manuals, community-developed tuning guides, and the "MoterNet" Android application.

### 1. Official Manuals & Parameter Lists (PDF)
The official documentation is split into two primary files: the hardware manual and the parameter adjustment guide.

*   **Fardriver Controller Manual (Hardware/Wiring):** Covers technical specifications, wiring diagrams (Hall sensors, throttle, brakes), and error codes.
    *   [Download from Official Site (far-driver.com)](https://www.far-driver.com/download/)
    *   [View on Scribd](https://www.scribd.com/document/524444444/Fardriver-Controller-Manual)
*   **Parameter Adjustment Instructions (The "Parameter List"):** This is the core document for tuning. It explains every setting in the app, including Phase Current, Line Current, Field Weakening, and PID settings.
    *   [Official Parameter Guide (PDF)](https://www.far-driver.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/The-adjustment-instructions-of-the-control-parameters-of-the-Fardriver-controller.pdf)
*   **Community "Cheat Sheet" (v2.4):** A highly recommended PDF guide by the community (often cited by Surron/Talaria tuners) that simplifies the factory instructions.
    *   [Far Driver Tuning v2.4 (Dropbox Link)](https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/84rb0byhjqimjc1fmx4jg/Far-Driver-Tuning-v2.4.pdf?rlkey=lolpiq43b29t5aqcaf2lsuc25&dl=0)

### 2. Android App ("MoterNet")
The app is used to communicate with the controller via Bluetooth.[1]
*   **App Name:** Often listed as **MoterNet** or **FarDriver** in app stores.
*   **Download:** 
    *   **Android:** Available on the [Google Play Store](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.fardriver.moternet) or as an APK from the [official website](https://www.far-driver.com/download/).
    *   **iOS:** Available on the Apple App Store.
*   **Setup Tip:** You must register with an email to receive a verification code. Ensure Bluetooth and GPS (Location) are enabled on your phone, or the app will not "bind" to the controller.[2]

### 3. Key Tuning Parameters & Guide
When using the app, follow these critical steps for a safe setup:

| Parameter | Description | Recommended Action |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Auto Learn** | Calibrates the controller to the motor's phase angle.[2] | **Mandatory.** Run this first with the wheel off the ground. |
| **Pole Pairs** | Number of magnet pairs in the motor.[2] | Must match your motor (e.g., QS138 is 5 pole pairs). |
| **Max Phase Current** | Controls low-end torque.[3] | Do not exceed the controller's factory limit to avoid burnout.[4][3] |
| **Max Line Current** | Controls top-end power/battery draw.[3][5][4] | Set this based on your battery's BMS discharge limit. |
| **Field Weakening** | Increases top speed beyond rated RPM. | Increase gradually; excessive values cause motor instability. |
| **Throttle Low/High** | Sets the voltage range for the throttle.[4][2][3] | Usually 0.8V (Low) to 4.2V (High). |

### 4. Troubleshooting Common Errors
*   **MOE / OVER:** Usually indicates excessive field weakening or a PID loop that is too aggressive.
*   **Throttle Error:** Check if your "Low Threshold" is set too low (should be ~0.2V above the idle voltage shown in the app's graph).
*   **Communication Failed:** Ensure the controller is powered on (Key/Ignition wire must have battery voltage) and the Bluetooth dongle is flashing.

Sources:
[1] alicdn.com (https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQHQKqjJpTmSuEDNKonodWTP5BuLV9EszZUM3c0MSn1fFl_aUhWhii14k5ZPIi0eILgkkGQth-2pIHtEqEKbyNJVo3A-5PfoRBShNInDjaj1ttcUIUnSNuqQGqnp5Zfm0YBDDo83oq66mt42gd6PWKsMZOHFmnf1mCVOJD8=)

messages.content:
Based on the official FarDriver (MoterNet) Android application and tuning guides, here is the comprehensive parameter list specifically detailed for the **FarDriver ND72450** motor controller. 

The ND72450 is rated for **72V nominal**, **200A Line (Battery) Current**, and **450A Phase (Motor) Current**. 

*Note: Default values can vary slightly depending on the firmware version or the vendor who flashed the controller. The ranges provided are the hardcoded limits within the app for this specific hardware.*

---

### 1. Basic Settings (Power & Voltage)
These parameters dictate the core power delivery and battery limitations.

| Exact Parameter Name | Default | Min / Max Range | Unit | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Line Curr** | 100 | 0 / 200 | A (Amps) | **Max Battery Current:** The maximum continuous current drawn from your battery. Set this strictly based on your battery's BMS continuous discharge rating. Exceeding your BMS limit will cause the battery to shut down. |
| **Phase Curr** | 250 | 0 / 450 | A (Amps) | **Max Motor Current:** Dictates low-end torque and acceleration punch. Higher values give aggressive take-offs but generate significant heat in the motor and controller. |
| **Rated Volt** | 72 | 48 / 72 | V (Volts) | **System Voltage:** The nominal voltage of your battery pack. The ND72450 is optimized for 72V (20S Lithium-ion) but can run lower voltages. |

### 2. Motor & Hall Sensor Settings
These parameters are critical for the controller to understand and spin the motor correctly. **Incorrect settings here can damage the motor.**

| Exact Parameter Name | Default | Min / Max Range | Unit | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Motor Poles** | 4 | 1 / 32 | Pairs | **Pole Pairs:** The number of magnetic pole *pairs* inside your motor (Total Magnets ÷ 2). E.g., a QS138 90H motor has 5 pole pairs. |
| **Hall Angle** | 60 | 0 / 360 | Degrees | **Sensor Phase Angle:** The electrical angle of the hall sensors. Usually determined automatically via the "Auto Learn" function. Do not guess this value. |
| **Exchange Hall** | 0 | 0 / 1 | Binary | Swaps the hall sensor phase reading sequence. Used if the motor spins backward or stutters. (0 = Normal, 1 = Swapped). |
| **Exchange Phase** | 0 | 0 / 1 | Binary | Swaps the physical motor phase wire sequence internally. Used to reverse motor direction without rewiring. |
| **Auto Learn** | 0 | 0 / 1 | Action | **Self-Calibration:** Set to 1 and twist the throttle slightly. The motor will spin slowly and calculate the exact Hall Angle and phase sequence. |

### 3. Throttle & Speed Limits
Controls how the bike reacts to your wrist input and sets the 3-speed switch parameters.

| Exact Parameter Name | Default | Min / Max Range | Unit | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Throttle Low** | 0.90 | 0.00 / 2.00 | V (Volts) | **Deadzone start:** The voltage where the motor begins to spin. Usually set ~0.15V higher than the resting voltage of your throttle to prevent accidental creeping. |
| **Throttle High** | 4.20 | 3.00 / 5.00 | V (Volts) | **100% Throttle:** The voltage at wide-open throttle. If set higher than your throttle can output, you will never reach 100% power. |
| **Accel** | 64 | 16 / 224 | Value | **Acceleration Curve / Throttle Response:** Lower numbers (e.g., 32) mean a smooth, soft ramp-up. Higher numbers (e.g., 128+) give a snappy, aggressive, "jerky" throttle response. |
| **Decel** | 32 | 16 / 224 | Value | **Deceleration Curve:** How quickly the controller drops power when you release the throttle. |
| **Gear 1 (Low)** | 40 | 10 / 100 | % | **Speed/Power Limit for Gear 1:** Limits the RPM/Phase current when the 3-speed switch is in the lowest position. |
| **Gear 2 (Mid)** | 70 | 10 / 100 | % | **Speed/Power Limit for Gear 2:** The middle switch position limit. |
| **Gear 3 (High)** | 100 | 10 / 100 | % | **Speed/Power Limit for Gear 3:** The highest switch position limit. |
| **Reverse Speed** | 20 | 5 / 50 | % | **Reverse Limit:** Limits speed when the reverse wire is engaged. |

### 4. Field Weakening (High-Speed Tuning)
Field weakening (FW) pushes the motor past its natural physical RPM limit by injecting counter-current into the stator. Use with extreme caution.

| Exact Parameter Name | Default | Min / Max Range | Unit | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Weakening** | 0 | 0 / 100 | A (Amps) | **Field Weakening Current:** The amount of phase current dedicated to weakening the magnetic field to increase top speed. Setting this too high causes massive heat and can result in the controller shutting down at high speeds (MOE fault). |
| **Start RPM** | 4000 | 0 / 8000 | RPM | **FW Engagement Point:** The motor RPM at which Field Weakening begins to apply. Should be set just below the motor's natural max RPM without FW. |

### 5. Regen Braking (EBS - Electronic Braking System)
Controls how much power is pushed back into the battery when braking or coasting.

| Exact Parameter Name | Default | Min / Max Range | Unit | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **EBS Level** | 0 | 0 / 10 | Level | **Braking Force:** The intensity of electronic braking when pulling the brake lever. 0 is off. Higher numbers brake harder. |
| **Slide Regen** | 0 | 0 / 10 | Level | **Off-Throttle Regen:** Acts like engine braking on a gas motorcycle. Engages regen immediately when you roll off the throttle. |
| **Max Regen Curr** | 20 | 0 / 60 | A (Amps) | **Max Recharge Current:** The maximum current pushed back into the battery. *Must not exceed your battery BMS's max charge limit*, or the BMS will trip and the controller will lose power. |

### 6. Protection & Cutoffs
Crucial safety settings to protect the controller, motor, and battery.

| Exact Parameter Name | Default | Min / Max Range | Unit | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Under Volt** | 63.0 | 40.0 / 80.0 | V (Volts) | **Low Voltage Cutoff (LVC):** Controller stops pulling power when battery drops to this voltage. For a 72V (20S) battery, this is usually set around 60V–63V to prevent deep discharging. |
| **Over Volt** | 88.0 | 72.0 / 95.0 | V (Volts) | **High Voltage Cutoff (HVC):** Shuts down the system if voltage spikes (usually during heavy Regen braking on a full battery). The ND72450 hardware max is ~90V. |
| **Controller Temp** | 100 | 60 / 120 | °C | **Controller Thermal Rollback:** The controller will start reducing power if its internal heatsink reaches this temperature to prevent MOSFET failure. |
| **Motor Temp** | 120 | 80 / 150 | °C | **Motor Thermal Rollback:** If your motor has a temp sensor (usually KTY83/122 or NTC10K) wired to the controller, power will reduce when the motor gets this hot to prevent melting the winding lacquer or demagnetizing the magnets. |

### ⚠️ Pro-Tips for Tuning the ND72450 via App:
1. **Always run "Auto Learn" first** with the rear wheel suspended in the air. Never attempt to ride the bike before completing this step.
2. **Save your defaults:** Before changing *anything*, go through every page in the app and take screenshots of the factory parameters.
3. **Phase to Line Ratio:** A standard safe rule of thumb is keeping Phase Current roughly 2x to 2.5x higher than Line Current (e.g., 200A Line / 450A Phase). Setting Phase Current too high relative to Line Current can cause stuttering off the line.
